name: InfinitiWarrior
tagline: Developing for small startups, public institutions, and personal projects.
about: I am a versatile developer and junior pentester with experience working on solutions for public institutions. My work spans both front-end and back-end development, with a strong focus on building secure, reliable, and maintainable systems.

I enjoy tackling a wide range of technical challenges and learning new technologies as I go. As a jack-of-all-trades, I adapt quickly, explore modern frameworks, and continuously develop my skills while keeping a solid foundation in core software engineering and cybersecurity principles.

projects.name: binary-reconstructor
projects.description: Static analysis tool that lifts stripped x86_64 ELF binaries into readable C-like pseudocode through real dataflow analysis — SSA-form IR, CFG recovery from cmp/jcc pairs, GOT-indirect import resolution for -fno-plt binaries. No symbol table required; handles hardened/PIE binaries that trip up Ghidra.

projects.name: azemu
projects.description: A local, open-source emulator for Azure, Entra ID, and Intune — Graph/ARM/Intune APIs, real OAuth2 token issuance and enforcement, and Docker-backed VM simulation with billing tracking, for dev/test/learning without touching a real tenant.

projects.name: systemd-audit
projects.description: A rogue systemd unit detector. Baselines every unit file, drop-in override, and transient runtime unit on a Linux system, then flags new, modified, masked, or suspiciously transient changes — the persistence surface most file-integrity tools miss.

projects.name: git-annales
projects.description: A git repository forensic time-traveler. Walks the full commit graph to reconstruct a security timeline — secrets that ever existed, dependency mutations, config drift, and suspicious commit patterns — instead of only looking at HEAD.

projects.name: pharos
projects.description: An adversarial WiFi fuzzing framework — byte-by-byte IEEE 802.11 beacon frame construction and mutation, with hostapd integration and packet injection, for testing wireless stacks against malformed frames.

projects.name: Vigil
projects.description: Typed, async/await-native authentication middleware for Node.js — a focused replacement for the middleware Passport.js used to own, not a full auth platform. 172 tests across 19 packages.
